title: Gloria Steinem Dies at 92, Leaving a Feminist Legacy
seoTitle: Gloria Steinem dies at 92 and leaves feminist legacy
subtitle: The founder of Ms. magazine passed away in New York, surrounded by those who admired her.
excerpt: Journalist and activist Gloria Steinem died at 92 in New York. Her trajectory includes founding Ms. magazine and establishing feminist organizations.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Folha de S.Paulo, CBN, CNN Brasil
contentHtml:
Gloria Steinem passed away peacefully at her New York home, surrounded by loved ones, on Wednesday, September 2, 2026. The news, released by the writer's own foundation, generated significant repercussions, marking the end of a life dedicated to feminism and gender equality.

What Gloria Steinem's Death Represents for the Feminist Movement

Steinem was a leading figure in the second wave of feminism, using journalism to bring to light issues such as reproductive rights, equal pay, and domestic violence. Her work helped transform the debate on “women's issues” into a political and cultural agenda in the United States.

Journalistic Contributions and the Creation of Ms. Magazine

In 1971, alongside Dorothy Pitman Hughes, Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine, the first major publication owned and run by women. The magazine addressed topics previously considered taboo, such as abortion, sexuality, and women's political participation, influencing generations of readers.

Organizations and Initiatives Founded by Steinem

In addition to Ms., Steinem helped establish the National Women's Political Caucus, the Coalition of Labor Union Women, the Women's Media Center, and the Ms. Foundation for Women. She also instituted Take Our Daughters to Work Day, which spread globally as a way to combat gender stereotypes.

Recognition and International Legacy

In 2013, then-President Barack Obama awarded Steinem the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the highest civilian honor in the United States. Her face and name became global symbols of the fight for women's rights, inspiring films, documentaries, and plays that narrate her journey.

How Steinem's Memory Can Inspire Brazil

Although her work was centered in the United States, the causes Steinem championed – equal pay, combating violence against women, and the right to abortion – are equally relevant in the Brazilian context. Feminist organizations in Brazil continue to cite her example when promoting awareness campaigns and lobbying for legislative changes.

With information from Folha de S.Paulo, CBN, CNN Brasil.
